# Broccoli Secure Gateway Companion — Android bootstrap build

**Bootstrap debug APK generated by GitHub Actions** (JDK 17 / Gradle 8.9 / AGP 8.7.3 / SDK 35).

## Immediate installation

1. In the `Grasshopper` repository, open **Actions → Build Broccoli Gateway Companion APK (preview)** and select the latest **successful** run.
2. At the bottom of the run page, download the artifact named `broccoli-gateway-bootstrap-apk-...`, extract the ZIP, then tap `app-debug.apk` on Android. You may need to authorize app installation from your file manager. Do not grant unrelated permissions.
3. The resulting **bootstrap preview package ID** is `org.broccoli.companion.gateway.bootstrap`. The **release ID** will be `org.broccoli.companion.gateway`, allowing your future privately signed release to coexist without uninstalling the preview.
4. The app can display pairing and biometric approval UI. It **will not pair** until a verified, phone-reachable HTTPS gateway has been installed on Grasshopper. This is intentional. Do not enter a Google password through the existing raw-IP HTTP noVNC viewer.
5. The bootstrap APK does **not** contain Firebase Cloud Messaging credentials or send push. First real-device acceptance requires backend integration and secure Android origin validation.

## Self-signed permanent version — Android phone

Use the separately supplied `termux_broccoli_companion_signing_prep.sh` script:

```bash
bash termux_broccoli_companion_signing_prep.sh --audit
bash termux_broccoli_companion_signing_prep.sh --prepare     # only with your confirmation
bash termux_broccoli_companion_signing_prep.sh --create-key  # interactive, never upload the private key
bash termux_broccoli_companion_signing_prep.sh --verify-key
```

Existing user-owned release keystores should be inventoried before making a new identity. Do **not** accidentally delete or overwrite one. Store a password and encrypted offline backup that you control. The preview is signed with a **transient CI debug key**; this cannot be used for consistent production upgrades, hence the separate package IDs.

Native Android ARM Gradle builds need SDK 35, Java 17, Gradle 8.9 and an Android-compatible `aapt2`, signing tools and sufficient storage. The audit checks what is currently installed. Do not assume that an x86 Linux Android SDK downloaded into Termux can execute on ARM. A later option is to build an **unsigned release APK** on public GitHub Actions, download to your phone and **sign locally**, keeping the private keystore completely off GitHub.

## Safety & status

- CI jobs run **zero cloud provider create/update/delete operations**. Standard public-repository GitHub-hosted Actions runners are used for a project build.
- Debug APK has no notification backend and should be treated as **developer preview**, not production-ready identity manager.
- No owner credential, private release signing key, OAuth callback, site tokens or password is included in source, APK, job logs or artifacts.
- Android Keystore P-256 authentication is per-operation with `BIOMETRIC_STRONG` and cannot be substituted by just clicking an authorization button.
- Gateway backend in supplied v0.2 archive has **not** been deployed on the live Grasshopper public noVNC URL.

## Planned production milestones

1. Gateway HTTPS hostname reachable from the physical phone and independently tested; authenticated noVNC ingress denying legacy unauthenticated bypass.
2. Pairing, biometric proof, expiring one-time grants, WebSocket revocation tested on actual Android.
3. Independently verified site-login completion before autonomous task resumption.
4. Optional Firebase Spark/no-cost project and signed companion push integration, authorized by owner.
5. Unsigned release via GitHub → owner-held signing on Android → repeatable update acceptance; sign once, keep the same keystore for upgrades.
